desc:
Support tone of voice and policy rules decide how every customer reply sounds and what it promises. Ecom Swift LLC writes them down in plain words, as a ready-to-paste instruction document your reply tools and your team can follow.

## What are support tone of voice and policy rules?

They are a written set of instructions that describe how your replies should sound and what they may say. The tone part covers wording to use and avoid, greetings and sign-offs. The policy part covers what can be promised on refunds, shipping and warranty, and which cases must go to a person. Reply tools and new staff read the same rules.

## Why unwritten rules cause inconsistent replies

When rules live in the owner's head, every reply depends on who writes it. One agent apologizes warmly, another is curt. One offers a refund, another refuses the same case. A helper without rules guesses, and its guesses can be too generous, too strict or simply off-brand.

Mistakes in this area cost money. A wrong promise about a refund or delivery can become a dispute. Writing the rules down once turns a pile of habits into something you can teach, test and improve.

## How clear rules improve every reply

Good rules make replies faster to write and safer to send. Agents stop debating wording and tools stop improvising. Customers receive the same answer to the same question regardless of who responds.

Rules also set limits. A list of cases that must go to a person, such as legal threats, safety claims or very large refunds, keeps sensitive decisions with people. Rules cannot prevent every wrong answer, but they reduce the odds sharply and make errors easy to trace to a line you can change.

## What a complete rule set includes

- A short description of your brand voice, in words your team recognizes.
- Words and phrases to use, and words and phrases to avoid.
- Greeting and sign-off wording for different situations.
- Policy lines for refunds, returns, shipping and warranty.
- Clear limits on what may be promised.
- A list of cases that always go to a person.
- Guidance for angry, confused or very short customer messages.
- Model replies that show the rules in action.
- Text formatted to paste into your reply tool.
- A one page summary for your team.

## How we do it

We interview you about how you want to sound and read a sample of your past replies to hear how you actually sound. We collect your policies and mark where they are unclear or contradict each other. We then write the rules, turn them into instruction text and test them on sample questions, adjusting the wording where the results are off.

The Basic package delivers a one page tone guide from your own replies. The Standard package adds policy rules and instruction text tested on sample questions. The Premium package covers more policy areas, lists the cases that must go to a person, adds model replies and a team summary sheet. This is practical writing for support work. It is not legal advice, and any legal terms in your policies should be checked by a qualified person.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Share replies you are proud of and some you regret.
- State what an agent may offer without asking.
- Keep each rule short enough to apply in seconds.
- Review the rules when policies change.

**Avoid:**
- Writing rules full of exceptions and vague words.
- Copying a competitor voice.
- Forbidding so many words that replies sound stiff.
- Letting old and new policies sit in the same document.
- Treating the rules as finished forever.

## Who it suits

A founder preparing to hire a first support agent. A store about to switch on a reply helper that must speak in its own voice. A team whose agents answer the same question in different ways.

## What we need from you

Samples of past replies, your current policies in any format and a few minutes to describe your brand. We do not need any passwords. If you use a specific reply tool, tell us which, and we will format the instructions for it.
